get_coordinate_info.description: Find out which country and timezone a latitude and longitude fall in, with a map link for the point. Works for anywhere on Earth, not just under a satellite. No API key required.
get_coordinate_info.name: get_coordinate_info

parameters.description: Latitude in decimal degrees, between -90 and 90. Negative is south of the equator.
parameters.name: latitude

parameters.description: Longitude in decimal degrees, between -180 and 180. Negative is west of Greenwich.
parameters.name: longitude

country_code.description: Two-letter country code for the point, or empty when it is over international waters.

latitude.description: Latitude of the point, in degrees.

longitude.description: Longitude of the point, in degrees.

map_url.description: Google Maps link centred on the point.

timezone_id.description: IANA timezone at the point, e.g. 'America/Los_Angeles'.

utc_offset_hours.description: That timezone's offset from UTC in hours, as reported by the API.

get_ground_location.description: Answer 'where is the ISS, and what is it over?' in one step: its position plus the country, timezone and map link for the point on the ground directly below it. The country is empty when it is over open ocean. No API key required.
get_ground_location.display_name: Get what a satellite is flying over
get_ground_location.display_str_template: Get what the satellite is flying over.
get_ground_location.name: get_ground_location

parameters.description: Which satellite to look up. Defaults to the International Space Station (NORAD catalog number 25544), the only satellite the API tracks today.
parameters.name: satellite_id

parameters.description: Optional. The moment to report on, past or future. Leave empty for right now.
parameters.name: at_time

parameters.description: Units for altitude, speed and footprint. Kilometres by default; latitude and longitude are always in decimal degrees.
parameters.name: units

get_ground_location.result_str_template: Retrieved the satellite's position and the place below it.

location.description: The point on the ground directly below it.

country_code.description: Two-letter country code for the point, or empty when it is over international waters.

latitude.description: Latitude of the point, in degrees.

longitude.description: Longitude of the point, in degrees.

map_url.description: Google Maps link centred on the point.

timezone_id.description: IANA timezone at the point, e.g. 'America/Los_Angeles'.

utc_offset_hours.description: That timezone's offset from UTC in hours, as reported by the API.

altitude.description: Height above the ground, in the requested units.

daynum.description: The same instant as a Julian date.

footprint.description: Diameter of the circle of ground the satellite is above the horizon for, in the requested units.

latitude.description: Latitude of the point below the satellite, in degrees.

longitude.description: Longitude of the point below the satellite, in degrees.

satellite_id.description: NORAD catalog number of the satellite, e.g. 25544.

solar_latitude.description: Latitude of the point the Sun is directly over.

solar_longitude.description: Longitude of the point the Sun is directly over.

time.description: The same instant as an ISO 8601 UTC date-time.

timestamp.description: The instant this position is for, in Unix seconds.

units.description: Which units the distances above are in.

velocity.description: Speed over the ground, in the requested units per hour.

visibility.description: Whether the satellite is lit: 'daylight' (in sunlight over a daylit ground), 'visible' (in sunlight over a dark ground, so it can be seen from below) or 'eclipsed' (in the Earth's shadow).

get_ground_track.description: Follow the path a satellite traces over the Earth: an evenly spaced run of up to ten positions from a starting time. Say when to start, how far apart the readings should be and how many you want: the times are worked out for you. No API key required.
get_ground_track.name: get_ground_track

parameters.description: Which satellite to look up. Defaults to the International Space Station (NORAD catalog number 25544), the only satellite the API tracks today.
parameters.name: satellite_id

parameters.description: Optional. When the track should start. Leave empty to start from now.
parameters.name: start_time

parameters.description: How far apart the readings are. The ISS circles the Earth in about 93 minutes, so 10 minutes traces most of an orbit across five readings.
parameters.name: interval_minutes

parameters.description: How many readings to return, including the one at the start time. The API allows up to ten per request.
parameters.name: points

parameters.description: Units for altitude, speed and footprint. Kilometres by default; latitude and longitude are always in decimal degrees.
parameters.name: units

positions.description: The positions along the track, earliest first.

solar_longitude.description: Longitude of the point the Sun is directly over.

time.description: The same instant as an ISO 8601 UTC date-time.

units.description: Which units the distances above are in.

velocity.description: Speed over the ground, in the requested units per hour.

visibility.description: Whether the satellite is lit: 'daylight' (in sunlight over a daylit ground), 'visible' (in sunlight over a dark ground, so it can be seen from below) or 'eclipsed' (in the Earth's shadow).

start_time.description: The same instant as an ISO 8601 UTC date-time.

start_timestamp.description: The instant the track starts at, in Unix seconds.

get_positions.description: Get a satellite's position at up to ten separate moments in one request, for example the times a pass was reported, or the same minute on ten different days. No API key required.
get_positions.name: get_positions

parameters.description: Which satellite to look up. Defaults to the International Space Station (NORAD catalog number 25544), the only satellite the API tracks today.
parameters.name: satellite_id

parameters.description: The moments to report positions for, up to ten. Each entry can be a date and time (2026-08-15T04:53:45Z) or a Unix timestamp in seconds.
parameters.name: times

parameters.description: Units for altitude, speed and footprint. Kilometres by default; latitude and longitude are always in decimal degrees.

get_tle.description: Get the satellite's current two-line element set (the orbital data tracking software needs to predict passes), both as separate fields and as the plain three-line block those tools expect. No API key required.
get_tle.name: get_tle

parameters.description: Which satellite to look up. Defaults to the International Space Station (NORAD catalog number 25544), the only satellite the API tracks today.
parameters.name: satellite_id

header.description: The element set's title line, e.g. 'ISS (ZARYA)'.

line1.description: First line of the two-line element set.

line2.description: Second line of the two-line element set.

requested_time.description: When it was requested, as an ISO 8601 UTC date-time.

requested_timestamp.description: When it was requested, in Unix seconds.

satellite_id.description: NORAD catalog number of the satellite.

text.description: Header and both lines joined by newlines: the plain-text TLE block tracking libraries read.

tle_time.description: When it was issued, as an ISO 8601 UTC date-time.

tle_timestamp.description: When this element set was issued, in Unix seconds. Element sets are refreshed every few hours.

list_satellites.description: List every satellite Where the ISS At? tracks, with the NORAD catalog number the other actions take. Currently that is the International Space Station. No API key required.
list_satellites.name: list_satellites

satellite_id.description: NORAD catalog number. Use it with the position, ground track and TLE actions.

description: Track the International Space Station with Where the ISS At?: where it is right now, where it was or will be at any moment, the path it traces over the Earth, the country and timezone it is flying over, and the orbital elements (TLE) pass-prediction tools need. No account or API key required.
